The Santa Rosa County Sheriff's Office has not yet released additional details about the victim or the circumstances surrounding the incident. The case remains under investigation. Hit-and-run…
item.content:encoded:
A Milton resident is facing charges after authorities say he struck and killed a woman with his vehicle then fled the scene, according to WKRG News 5.

The Santa Rosa County Sheriff's Office has not yet released additional details about the victim or the circumstances surrounding the incident. The case remains under investigation.

Hit-and-run fatalities are treated as felonies in Florida, with potential charges ranging from vehicular homicide to leaving the scene of a fatal crash. Anyone with information about the incident is urged to contact the Santa Rosa County Sheriff's Office.

item.title: George County Schools investigates fake social media impersonation of teacher
item.dc:creator: newsroom

The fake page was brought to the attention of George County School District officials, who confirmed the account does not belong to the…
item.content:encoded:
School administrators in George County, Mississippi have launched an investigation after discovering someone created a fraudulent social media account impersonating one of their teachers, according to WKRG News 5.

The fake page was brought to the attention of George County School District officials, who confirmed the account does not belong to the actual educator. While details remain limited, the discovery has prompted district leadership to look into who created the impostor account and for what purpose.

The incident highlights growing concerns about social media fraud and identity theft targeting educators. School districts across the country have dealt with similar cases where unauthorized accounts have been created in teachers' names, sometimes used to spread misinformation or harass school staff.

George County School District has not released additional information about the investigation or whether any disciplinary action will result from the discovery.

item.content:encoded: Residents across Okaloosa County should expect to hear significant detonation sounds next week as Hurlburt Field conducts explosive demolition training exercises. According to an Air Force release, the training will run from 7 a.m. to 3 p.m. and is part of routine military operations at the base. The blasts may be audible across a wide area, so residents are being notified in advance to avoid confusion or concern about the source of the noise. The Air Force has not specified which days the training will occur, so residents should monitor local military and emergency management channels for exact dates.

item.content:encoded: Penascola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- The University of West Florida has been named one of sixteen new national Centers of Excellence for Maritime Workforce Training, a designation from the U-S Maritime Administration. UWF supports more than a thousand active students working with local shipbuilders and manufacturers, including American Magic and Jupiter Bach. Dean Mohamed Khabou says UWF is expanding its engineering programs to meet growing demand from Gulf Coast maritime employers. The recognition comes as Northwest Florida sees rapid growth in shipbuilding, including projects like Birdon's new facility at the Port of Pensacola.

item.title: PPD's Mike Wood on Fire Suppression Tools, Flock Camera Fallout, and Another Escaped Pig
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Pensacola Police PIO Mike Wood joined Pensacola's Morning News on Thursday after returning from a week at a national conference for public information officers, where departments from around the country compared notes on everything from Flock cameras to teen takeovers to lessons learned from the deadly flooding in…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Pensacola Police PIO Mike Wood joined Pensacola's Morning News on Thursday after returning from a week at a national conference for public information officers, where departments from around the country compared notes on everything from Flock cameras to teen takeovers to lessons learned from the deadly flooding in Texas earlier this year.


Pushing for Fire Suppression Devices in Patrol Cars

Wood has been promoting a small aerosol device called a fire suppression tool that he believes could give officers a real edge at house fires, where police are often first on scene, sometimes minutes ahead of the fire department. The device releases an aerosol within eight seconds of being thrown into a burning room and can knock down a fire in about 30 seconds, according to Wood, without depleting oxygen in the space. He compared it to Narcan and defibrillators already carried in patrol cars, noting the device has a 15-year shelf life regardless of temperature. Wood was careful to note it wouldn't replace the fire department, but could buy critical time for people to escape or for firefighters to finish the job once they arrive.


Flock Cameras Solved Burglary at NASCAR Driver's Home

Wood shared another example of how Flock cameras have helped solve crimes locally, this one tied to NASCAR driver Greg Biffle. After Biffle's wife and two young children died in a plane crash in December, someone broke into his home and stole trophies, cash, and other items. Wood says a Flock camera helped investigators locate and arrest the suspect. He acknowledged the frustration many officers feel now that the cameras are offline following the state's order to remove them from state road rights-of-way, but said police have to listen when the community raises concerns about how a tool like this operates. Wood also addressed concerns about Flock's data being held by a private company rather than a government system like NCIC or DAVID, the databases law enforcement already uses for driver's license and vehicle information, saying that distinction is part of what's driving public unease even though officers face serious consequences, including losing their jobs, for misusing either system.


Another Pig on the Loose

In a lighter moment, Wood recapped PPD's third pig rescue of the year. Officers managed to get the runaway pig into a patrol car, but he didn't want to leave the air conditioning once they arrived to reunite him with his owner. Deputies eventually coaxed him out with double stuffed Oreos, and it took two pairs of handcuffs to get the job done.


Cop Myth: Federal Agencies "Taking Over" a Case

Wood also debunked a common TV trope, the idea that federal or state agencies swoop in and clash with local police over jurisdiction when they take over a case. In reality, Wood says local departments are usually glad to hand off cases to agencies with broader reach and steeper penalties available, and there's rarely any pushback at all.

item.content:encoded: Santa Rosa County, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Governor Ron DeSantis has awarded Santa Rosa County five-hundred-twenty-five-thousand dollars to expand Whiting Aviation Park and protect land around Naval Air Station Whiting Field. County officials say the investment strengthens the region's growing aviation and defense industry, aiming to attract new businesses and high-paying jobs.

item.title: Deputies Seize Enough Fentanyl to Kill Over a Million People During Wedgwood Traffic Stop
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Escambia County, FL (NewsRadioa 92.3) -- A routine tag violation stop in the Wedgwood area turned into one of the Escambia County Sheriff's Office's larger fentanyl seizures this week, according to Sheriff Chip Simmons. Simmons says Deputy Thomas Hurley pulled the car over Wednesday night, then called in K-9 Deputy Colton Clark and his dog,…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County, FL (NewsRadioa 92.3) -- A routine tag violation stop in the Wedgwood area turned into one of the Escambia County Sheriff's Office's larger fentanyl seizures this week, according to Sheriff Chip Simmons.


Simmons says Deputy Thomas Hurley pulled the car over Wednesday night, then called in K-9 Deputy Colton Clark and his dog, Roland, named after one of the agency's fallen deputies. Roland alerted to the presence of drugs, and deputies say a search of the vehicle turned up 2,145 grams of fentanyl along with nearly $23,000 in cash.


Two men were arrested at the scene. Simmons identified them as 25-year-old Ramon Becerra Uribe and 25-year-old Adrian Medina-Ortiz, both charged with trafficking in fentanyl. Simmons says Becerra Uribe is also facing an additional charge for being in the country illegally.


Simmons used the seizure to underscore just how dangerous fentanyl is in even small quantities. Citing the DEA's benchmark of 2 milligrams as a potentially lethal dose, Simmons said the amount recovered from the car could theoretically represent more than a million lethal doses. He noted that fentanyl is frequently mixed into other drugs without users' knowledge, which he says is part of what makes it so deadly.


Simmons credited Deputy Hurley and K-9 Deputy Clark with the bust, saying their work last night likely saved lives.

item.content:encoded:
The University of West Florida football team has cracked the FCS national rankings following a 34-31 upset victory over No. 16 Southern Illinois last Thursday. The win earned UWF the Stats Perform FCS National Team of the Week honor and vaulted the Argonauts into the Stats Perform FCS Top 25 Poll.

The victory marked a significant milestone for the program, which defeated a ranked opponent in a closely contested matchup. The defensive effort and offensive execution in the win caught the attention of national evaluators, leading to the weekly team award.

UWF's breakthrough into the national rankings represents a major step forward for the Argonauts' season. The program will look to build on the momentum as they continue their FCS schedule.

Catherine Stewart Whitehead, a longtime Molino resident who dedicated her life to caring for others, passed away on August 28, 2026, at the age of 77. She was surrounded by her children and sister at the time of her death.

Whitehead was born and raised in Molino, where she spent her entire life in service to her community. She worked as a school bus driver and later owned and operated a day care, touching the lives of countless children and families throughout North Escambia County.

Services and other details are pending.

item.title: ECUA Reports 3,600 Gallon Sewage Spill on East Kingsfield Road
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Emerald Coast Utilities Authority dealt with a sanitary sewer overflow Wednesday morning on East Kingsfield Road after a contractor accidentally damaged a critical sewer line. The incident happened at 1425 East Kingsfield Road between 10:30 a.m. and 1 p.m., when the contractor bored through a force main — one of the large pipes that carries…
item.content:encoded: The Emerald Coast Utilities Authority dealt with a sanitary sewer overflow Wednesday morning on East Kingsfield Road after a contractor accidentally damaged a critical sewer line. The incident happened at 1425 East Kingsfield Road between 10:30 a.m. and 1 p.m., when the contractor bored through a force main — one of the large pipes that carries sewage under pressure through the system. A total of 3,600 gallons spilled, though ECUA crews were able to recover 3,500 gallons. ECUA did not immediately report any impact to customers or surrounding areas, but the authority typically notifies affected residents when overflows occur. Force main breaches are relatively serious incidents since they can require emergency repairs to restore service.

Participants should plan to arrive by 7:30 a.m. for check-in, with a mandatory safety briefing scheduled for 8:30 a.m. Shooting will begin at 9:00 a.m. at the Pace facility.

For registration details and to sign up before the deadline, interested shooters should contact the Tate Aggies softball program directly. The event typically draws competitors from across Santa Rosa County and the surrounding area.

item.title: Wet weekend ahead for Escambia County with rain chances rising Friday

While Thursday offers only a slight chance of showers, moisture will build considerably by Friday, when daily shower and thunderstorm chances will increase significantly across Escambia County. Scattered to…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola residents should prepare for increasing rain chances as the weekend approaches, according to National Weather Service forecasts. While Thursday offers only a slight chance of showers, moisture will build considerably by Friday, when daily shower and thunderstorm chances will increase significantly across Escambia County.

Scattered to numerous showers and storms are expected to continue through the weekend and into early next week, making it a good time to wrap up outdoor plans or move them indoors. Those planning outdoor activities should monitor the latest forecasts Friday morning, as storm timing and intensity could shift.

Residents are advised to have a way to receive weather alerts and to stay weather-aware as the system moves through the region.

item.dc:creator: newsroom

Adrian Dion Pettaway Jr., 25, received a 28-month sentence for distributing fentanyl, while Gindy Nicole Lacey, 49, was sentenced to 60 months in federal prison for her role in distributing methamphetamine,…
item.content:encoded:
Two Escambia County residents are heading to federal prison following convictions on drug distribution charges, according to court records.

Adrian Dion Pettaway Jr., 25, received a 28-month sentence for distributing fentanyl, while Gindy Nicole Lacey, 49, was sentenced to 60 months in federal prison for her role in distributing methamphetamine, tramadol, and fentanyl.

The sentences are part of ongoing federal enforcement efforts targeting opioid and drug trafficking in the area. Fentanyl distribution remains a priority for law enforcement agencies across Northwest Florida as the powerful synthetic opioid continues to fuel overdose deaths nationally and locally.

item.content:encoded: A traffic collision on Highway 29 in Molino Wednesday afternoon didn't result in any injuries, according to reports. An SUV struck a tractor and mower that was positioned in the right travel lane at the time of impact. Emergency responders arrived at the scene, but no injuries were reported from the crash. The circumstances that led to the collision remain under investigation. Highway 29 is a major route through North Escambia County, and such incidents involving farm equipment on roadways can create hazardous conditions for motorists unfamiliar with sharing the road with agricultural vehicles.

item.content:encoded:
Escambia County officials are planning a grand reopening celebration for a local kids' park following recent improvements to the facility. The event will include a ribbon-cutting ceremony to officially mark the completion of the renovation project, according to WKRG News 5.

While specific details about the park's location, the nature of the improvements, and the exact date of the grand reopening ceremony weren't immediately available, county officials say the upgrades are aimed at enhancing the recreational experience for children and families in the area.

The announcement comes as part of ongoing efforts by Escambia County to maintain and upgrade public parks and recreational facilities throughout the region. More information about the event, including the date and time, is expected to be released by county officials in the coming days.
